surface_summary: Alvin H. Benson, a Wall Street broker, is found shot in his home under mysterious circumstances. The investigation initially points suspicion at his dinner companion, Muriel St. Clair, and her fiancé, Captain Leacock, but the case is complicated by multiple suspects and conflicting alibis.
accepted_facts: Alvin Benson was shot through the forehead in his living-room.
His house was securely locked with barred windows and only the front door accessible.
Muriel St. Clair's gloves and handbag were found at the crime scene.
Captain Leacock confessed to the murder but his confession was inconsistent and later doubted.
inferred_conclusions: Muriel St. Clair was the murderer due to her personal items at the scene.
Captain Leacock was guilty based on his confession and motive of jealousy.
Leander Pfyfe was involved in the murder due to his suspicious presence and forged check.
mechanism_description: Major Anthony Benson, motivated by financial desperation and the desire to obtain jewels and securities held by his brother Alvin, planned and executed the murder. He entered Alvin’s house by tapping on the window, was admitted without Alvin’s toupee and false teeth, shot him at close range aiming deliberately at the forehead, then turned off the lights and left. He planted evidence to implicate others, including the dinner companion and Captain Leacock, but psychological analysis and alibi investigation revealed his guilt.
delivery_path: Major Benson learned Alvin’s schedule and that he would be home alone at midnight.
He tapped on the barred window and was admitted by Alvin without disguise.
He shot Alvin through the forehead from about five and a half feet away.
He turned off the lights and left the house before the housekeeper could hear.
He hid the jewels taken from Alvin’s safe in his own apartment.
He created false alibis and planted evidence to implicate Captain Leacock and others.
Investigators uncovered inconsistencies in alibis and found the hidden jewels and gun.
outcome_result: Major Anthony Benson was indicted and convicted for the murder of his brother Alvin H. Benson.

false_assumption.statement: The presence of Muriel St. Clair’s gloves and handbag at the crime scene proves she was the murderer.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The personal items were found in the victim’s living-room and she was known to have dined with him that night. It is natural to suspect someone whose belongings are at the scene.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It hides the fact that the victim himself brought her belongings home and that the real murderer planted these items to mislead the investigation.

supporting_points: He threatened Alvin Benson over his attentions to Muriel St. Clair.
He confessed to the murder, providing a detailed but inconsistent account.
He was seen near the crime scene at the relevant time.
He disposed of the murder weapon by throwing it into the river.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: His confession was full of contradictions and physical impossibilities, and psychological analysis showed he was unlikely to have committed the crime.

red_herrings.description: Gloves and handbag of Muriel St. Clair found at the crime scene suggest her presence and guilt.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Alvin Benson brought her belongings home after she left, and the items were planted to mislead.

red_herrings.description: Leander Pfyfe’s grey Cadillac was seen parked near the victim’s house on the night of the murder.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Pfyfe was in the city but had no involvement in the murder; he tried to mislead the investigation due to personal motives.

closed_circle.rationale: All had motive, opportunity, or suspicious behavior connected to the murder, and the investigation focused on this limited group.

discriminating_test.design: Investigators verify the alibi of Major Benson by checking the testimony of the elevator boy and other witnesses, and inspect the Major’s apartment for the murder weapon and stolen jewels. The presence of the gun and jewels in the Major’s locked apartment, combined with the broken alibi, confirms his opportunity and means.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The test reveals that Major Benson’s alibi is false and that he possessed the murder weapon and stolen jewels, proving his guilt.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Physical evidence of the gun and jewels in Major Benson’s apartment and credible witness testimony disproving his alibi.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given detailed descriptions of the crime scene, the suspects’ alibis, and the physical evidence such as the gun, jewels, and personal items. Psychological insights and inconsistencies in confessions are presented openly. The locked-room nature of the crime and the timing constraints are clearly outlined, allowing attentive readers to deduce the murderer’s identity by analyzing the alibis and motives.
